title: Epigenetic impact of a 1-week intensive multimodal group program for adolescents with multiple adverse childhood experiences.
authors: Kaliman P, Cosín-Tomás M, Madrid A, Roque López S, Llanez-Anaya E, Papale LA, Alisch RS, Davidson RJ.
summary: A one-week programme combining mindfulness, artistic expression and EMDR group therapy studied 44 adolescent girls with multiple adverse experiences. Forty-nine DNA-methylation loci differed with intervention; SIRT5 and TRAPPC2L changes correlated with trauma measures.
limitation: The programme has several components. Saliva methylation findings do not isolate EMDR; the study detected no intervention effect on intrinsic epigenetic age acceleration.

title: A Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial of Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing Therapy for Adults With Binge-Eating Disorder.
journal: The International journal of eating disorders
authors: Hatoum AH, Richard K, Burton AL, Rieger E, Touyz S, Abbott MJ.
summary: A 38-person pilot found greater reductions in binge-eating symptoms, days and frequency with an adapted ten-session EMDR protocol than waitlist, alongside improvements in selected anxiety and sleep outcomes.
limitation: Treatment completion was 68.8%, and several other outcomes did not improve. The small pilot and immediate post-treatment assessment support a larger trial rather than a settled treatment recommendation.

title: Eye movement desensitisation and reprocessing for post-traumatic stress in survivors of critical illness (EMERALD): a mixed-methods, randomised, single-blind, parallel group-controlled, feasibility trial.
authors: Bates A, Cusack R, Golding H, Moyses H, Southam H, Rushbrook S, Highfield J, Pattison N, Baldwin DS, Grocott MPW.
summary: The 40-person EMERALD trial in critical-illness survivors achieved 98% clinician-rated follow-up at 12 months. Exploratory PTSD symptom change favoured EMDR plus usual care by 14.1 points, with a 95% confidence interval of 6.2 to 22.0 points.
limitation: Feasibility, acceptability and safety were the primary objectives. The symptom estimate is hypothesis-generating and does not establish definitive treatment effectiveness.

title: Peer-delivered combined EMD and imagery rescripting for traumatized Chinese university students: a RCT.
authors: Fan H, Zhang J, Wang Y, Yang K, Wang Y, Yang X.
summary: Ninety-five university students were randomized to peer-delivered EMD plus imagery rescripting, imagery rescripting alone or care as usual. Four supervised sessions produced similar changes in depression and anxiety across groups; the combined intervention better maintained resilience gains at follow-up.
limitation: Trained peers received clinical supervision. The trial tested a combined intervention, with no significant group-by-time effects for depression, anxiety or self-efficacy.

title: Effects of eye movement desensitisation and reprocessing on depressive symptoms, stress and rumination in adolescents with depression: a randomised controlled trial.
authors: Zheng S, Shen Y, Geng F, Ye M, Song S, Wang R, Zhang S, Ou Y, Zhou X.
summary: Thirty adolescents aged 12–18 completed a comparison of EMDR plus an SSRI with an SSRI alone. Six sessions over two weeks were associated with larger improvements in depression, event-related stress and rumination.
limitation: Small trial with brief follow-up. This is adjunctive treatment alongside medication; it does not test an entertainment intervention.

authors: Daniëls M, Meewisse ML, Nugter A, Rameckers SA, Fassbinder E, Arntz A.

title: Stress and stress reactivity in posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) following eye movement desensitization (EMD): A randomized controlled trial.
journal: Journal of behavior therapy and experimental psychiatry
authors: Susanty E, Sijbrandij M, van der Mee DJ, Srisayekti W, Suparman Y, Huizink AC.
summary: Ninety-one adults with PTSD received eye-movement desensitization or memory retrieval alone. Both groups showed reduced stress reactivity; the study found no specific overall benefit of eye movements and inconsistent cortisol differences.
limitation: Saliva timing depended on participant adherence. This is the same registered component trial as the 2024 neurocognitive report, not an independent replication.

title: The Effectiveness of Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing Therapy on Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder Symptoms and Diagnostic Status in Patients with a Personality Disorder: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
authors: Hafkemeijer L, Hofman S, de Jongh A, de Roos D, van Velzen M, Starrenburg A, Slotema K.
summary: In 159 people with personality disorders, EMDR reduced PTSD symptoms more than a waitlist. Among participants with PTSD receiving EMDR, 65.5% no longer met the diagnosis after treatment and 73.1% at follow-up.
limitation: A waitlist does not control for therapeutic attention. The remission percentages describe the treated subgroup; they are not an absolute treatment effect or a general remission guarantee.

title: Treatment of traumatic birth experience with postpartum early eye movement desensitization and reprocessing therapy: a randomized clinical trial.
journal: American journal of obstetrics and gynecology
authors: Hendrix YMGA, van Pampus MG, Hofman A, Henrichs J, van der Horst HE, de Jongh A.
summary: Of 151 women randomised after a traumatic birth, 143 entered the reported intention-to-treat analysis. Two early postpartum EMDR sessions reduced self-reported and clinician-rated PTSD symptom severity compared with two telephone contacts; the reported raw symptom differences were 8.7 and 3.8 points respectively.
limitation: Clinician-diagnosed PTSD rates did not differ significantly. The abstract contains an inconsistent confidence-interval entry, so that interval is not reproduced here; follow-up was nine weeks postpartum.

title: Eye movement desensitization and reprocessing (EMDR) therapy compared to usual treatment for posttraumatic stress disorder in adults with psychosis in forensic settings: Randomized controlled trial.
journal: Psychological trauma : theory, research, practice and policy
authors: Every-Palmer S, Flewett T, Dean S, Hansby O, Freeland A, Weatherall M, Bell E.
summary: In 24 forensic patients with psychosis and PTSD, blinded assessments favoured EMDR over routine-care waitlist for clinician-rated PTSD symptoms. The estimated difference averaged across follow-ups was 11.4 points, with a 95% confidence interval of 1.3 to 21.4.
limitation: Recruitment was curtailed by pandemic restrictions, leaving a small sample. Psychotic symptoms and adverse events did not differ significantly, so effectiveness claims remain specific to the measured PTSD outcomes.

authors: Meneses AYM, Fernández-Gonzalo S, Vicente MJ.

authors: Novo P, Landin-Romero R, Radua J, Vicens V, Fernandez I, Garcia F, Pomarol-Clotet E, McKenna PJ, Shapiro F, Amann BL.
summary: In 20 people with bipolar disorder and trauma histories, EMDR improved depressive, hypomanic and trauma symptoms relative to usual care after treatment, using blinded outcome ratings.
limitation: The trial was small, with unequal dropout between groups. Most differences were not sustained at the 24-week assessment; this is an adjunctive pilot rather than evidence for replacing established bipolar treatment.

title: Brief eclectic psychotherapy v. eye movement desensitisation and reprocessing therapy for post-traumatic stress disorder: randomised controlled trial.
journal: The British journal of psychiatry : the journal of mental science
authors: Nijdam MJ, Gersons BP, Reitsma JB, de Jongh A, Olff M.
summary: In 140 people with PTSD, EMDR and brief eclectic psychotherapy produced similar final improvements; EMDR achieved improvement more rapidly during treatment.
